judge_framing.intro: You are grading a set of competing root-cause hypotheses, produced from a bug report and a snapshot of the codebase it describes, against the known true cause. Return STRICT JSON only — no prose, no markdown fences.
judge_framing.gt_heading: Ground-truth causal mechanisms the hypothesis set had to reach
judge_framing.negative_note: (none — this is a NEGATIVE task: the reported behavior is the code working as designed, so there is no defect to name and every hypothesis below goes to residue)
judge_framing.match_rule:
the SAME causal mechanism at the SAME location — not merely the same file, and not the same
   observable symptom. Two hypotheses naming one module for different reasons are different
   hypotheses; one naming the right mechanism at a slightly wrong line is a match. A hypothesis
   that restates the symptom ('the cache returns stale data') without naming a mechanism that
   would produce it is NOT a match for any item.
judge_framing.plausible_real:
a mechanism that genuinely could produce the reported symptom in this tree,
     and is not the ground-truth cause
judge_framing.noise:
a mechanism referring to code, config, or infrastructure that does not exist in this
     tree, or that could not produce the reported symptom
judge_framing.nitpick: real and correctly cited, but incapable of producing the reported symptom on its own

noise_floor_note: UNMEASURED — this module has not run its A-vs-A. compare.sh prints 'no measured noise floor' on the noise axis until it has, and per DESIGN.md a module with no measured band cannot screen. Run the A-vs-A FIRST, and run its SECOND ARM with --no-cache per DESIGN.md, or that arm replays the first arm's cached responses and the tie is fake. The three same-criteria facets need no special handling: the assembler injects a per-facet dimension line, so their prompts hash distinctly and do not share a cache entry.
